title: Work about work is a hand-off problem, not a people problem
dek: Surveys keep finding that more than half the week goes on coordination. The cause is not individual habits. It is the hand-offs nobody designed.
description: Why 'work about work' takes more than half of the knowledge worker's week, why focus campaigns and new tools underdeliver, and how to measure the hand-offs where time really disappears.

title: Flow efficiency: the number that explains why simple work takes weeks
dek: The work takes hours. The case takes weeks. Little's Law and a little queuing theory explain the gap, and how to close it.
description: What flow efficiency is, why knowledge work often sits at 5 to 15 per cent, how Little's Law links open work to cycle time, and how services firms can measure and reduce waiting.

title: Why automation programs stall, and how to choose your first five
dek: From RPA to generative AI, most pilots never pay back. The problem is rarely the technology. It is what gets chosen for automation.
description: Why 30 to 50 per cent of RPA projects and most generative AI pilots fail to deliver, why automating non-bottleneck steps rarely pays, and five tests for choosing automations that do.

title: How to build an automation business case your CFO will sign
dek: Hours saved are not dollars saved. A structure for sizing automation that survives a sceptical finance team, with a worked example.
description: A practical method for automation ROI: measured volumes, automation rate, adoption ramps, risk adjustment and full-life costs, plus how to separate capacity released from cash realised.

title: How to map work without monitoring people
dek: Process discovery and employee surveillance are different things. Here is what the law says in Australia, the UK and the US, and the design principles that keep them apart.
description: Workplace surveillance and privacy law for process discovery in Australia (NSW, ACT, Victoria, Privacy Act), the UK (ICO guidance) and the US (New York, California), and seven privacy-first design principles.
